newsitem.title: USA: U.S. presses for Zaire political solution.
newsitem.headline: U.S. presses for Zaire political solution.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday renewed its push for a political solution to Zaire's crisis and continued to rule out an American role in a proposed military intervention force.
"We are not prepared right now to sign on to a multinational force," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

Burns said U.S. officials would continue to discuss the multinational force idea, which was put forward by new Secretary General Kofi Annan and is backed by Paris. But he said Washington believes the political course being pursued at the moment is the right one.

"We think that actually what's being done is the best way to help the refugees and to stop the fighting -- to pursue the ceasefire and to continue to encourage the United Nations to deliver this humanitarian assistance," he said, adding: "We do not believe there is a military solution to the problems of Zaire."
Rebels have captured a swath of eastern Zaire, driving Rwandan Hutu refugees before them, and now threaten the government stronghold of Kisangani. They announced other advances on Tuesday.
Burns said the State Department has authorised the voluntary departure of the dependents of American diplomats and other U.S. government employees in the Zairean capital of Kinshasa.

Washington also issued a travel warning to Zaire, advising U.S. citizens to defer all travel there "due to the uncertain political and security situation there, and the potential for military and civil unrest throughout the country."
Burns said that Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has been spending considerable time on Zaire, holding several briefings a day on the fast-moving situation there.

Reflecting U.S. concern, he again issued a call for Laurent Kabila, the Zairean rebel leader, to accept a ceasefire proposal put forward by South Africa and the United States to end the fighting in eastern Zaire and to agree to talks with the Zairean government.
"That's the first order of business, to stop the fighting in eastern Zaire, now that the rebel alliance appears to be just outside the city limits of Kisangani," a key city, Burns said.
